log.text: Gholdengo used Make It Rain → Venusaur
Gholdengo used Make It Rain → Kingambit

decisions.rationale: Lead Whimsicott and Tyranitar to establish speed control while immediately overwriting Drought if Charizard-Mega-Y appears. Mega Tyranitar offers durable weather control; Gholdengo pressures Venusaur and ignores status disruption, while Arcanine is valuable for late-game pressure and Kingambit management.
decisions.notebook: Prioritize removing or overwriting opposing sun early. Preserve Mega Tyranitar when Venusaur and Kingambit can combine pressure. Use Gholdengo as a status-resistant attacker and track Make It Rain Special Attack drops. Raichu has Fake Out, Nuzzle, Encore, Lightning Rod, and Focus Sash; avoid Electric attacks and account for its Sash. Kingambit has Protect, Defiant, Chople Berry, and Sucker Punch; prefer reliable single-target pressure. Preserve Arcanine for the endgame.

decisions.rationale: Raichu + Venusaur gives Fake Out pressure into Whimsicott and immediate Grass pressure on Tyranitar/Milotic, while Raichu threatens Milotic and preserves Sash utility. Tauros covers Tyranitar and Arcanine; Kingambit is the dedicated Gholdengo answer.
decisions.notebook: Opponent’s revealed structure includes Sash Prankster Whimsicott disruption, Mega Tyranitar, Gholdengo, Flash Fire Arcanine, Competitive Milotic, and Life Orb Basculegion. Mega Charizard-Y/sun is a poor default into Tyranitar plus Flash Fire Arcanine and can amplify Arcanine’s Fire pressure. Preserve Kingambit for Gholdengo, but avoid relying on it alone against Arcanine. Venusaur Giga Drain into Mega Tyranitar in sand is only 35.3–62.3%, so do not assume a KO.

decisions.rationale: Switch Whimsicott to Gholdengo, whose Ghost typing blocks Fake Out and Good as Gold blocks Sleep Powder. Tyranitar protects to deny Venusaur’s likely pressure while preserving the Mega option and avoiding an exposed turn against faster foes. This establishes a safer next turn without unnecessarily committing the Mega.

decisions.rationale: Fake Out denies Prankster Tailwind/Taunt this turn, and Life Orb Sludge Bomb is a guaranteed OHKO damage range on Whimsicott after its Focus Sash is broken. This cleanly removes their speed-control lead; Tyranitar’s Rock Slide flinch chance is the principal disruption.
decisions.notebook: Opponent: Focus Sash Prankster Whimsicott with Tailwind/Taunt/Encore/Moonblast and no disclosed Protect; Mega Tyranitar; Metal Coat Good as Gold Gholdengo; Leftovers Competitive Milotic; Expert Belt Flash Fire Arcanine; Life Orb Swift Swim Basculegion. Preserve Kingambit for Gholdengo, but avoid leaving it unsupported versus Arcanine. Venusaur Giga Drain into Mega Tyranitar in sand is only 35.3–62.3%; do not assume a KO. Charizard-Y/sun is a poor default into Tyranitar plus Flash Fire Arcanine and can amplify Fire pressure.

decisions.rationale: Mega Tyranitar preserves the key defensive resource against Venusaur and future Kingambit while boosting Rock Slide pressure. Make It Rain hits both foes for strong spread damage, pairs with Rock Slide to heavily weaken or potentially remove Venusaur, and Gholdengo is immune to Fake Out and Sludge Bomb.

decisions.rationale: Raichu’s guaranteed-first Thunderbolt puts meaningful chip on Gholdengo while Venusaur pressures Mega Tyranitar with its strongest legal hit. Giga Drain is only a 35.3–62.3% range, so do not assume a KO, but splitting pressure best preserves follow-up cleanup lines with Kingambit and Tauros.
decisions.notebook: Opponent’s disclosed roster: Focus Sash Prankster Whimsicott (Tailwind/Taunt/Encore/Moonblast); Mega Tyranitar; Metal Coat Good as Gold Gholdengo; Leftovers Competitive Milotic; Expert Belt Flash Fire Arcanine; Life Orb Swift Swim Basculegion. Preserve Kingambit as a key Gholdengo answer, but avoid exposing it unsupported to Arcanine. Mega Tyranitar’s sand-boosted special bulk means Venusaur Life Orb Giga Drain is only 35.3–62.3%; plan for two-hit or Tauros cleanup rather than a one-shot. Gholdengo Make It Rain into Venusaur is 53.5–78.3% spread damage. Charizard-Y/sun is a poor default into Tyranitar plus Flash Fire Arcanine and can amplify opposing Fire pressure.

decisions.rationale: Bring Tauros to preserve Kingambit as the cleaner and Gholdengo answer. Intimidate immediately reduces Mega Tyranitar’s physical pressure, while Tauros threatens Tyranitar with Close Combat next turn; Venusaur has no legal action.
decisions.notebook: Raichu is down. Preserve Kingambit where possible as the primary Gholdengo answer, but do not leave it exposed to Arcanine without support. Tauros is valuable versus Mega Tyranitar through Intimidate and Close Combat. Gholdengo is immune to Raichu Fake Out and Venusaur Sludge Bomb via Good as Gold; Venusaur Giga Drain is the productive Tyranitar damage route. Mega Tyranitar’s sand-boosted special bulk means Giga Drain is generally a two-hit plan rather than a reliable OHKO.

decisions.rationale: Make It Rain guarantees the KO on Venusaur while also damaging Tauros; Tyranitar protects to avoid Tauros’s super-effective Fighting pressure and preserve it for the remaining board.

decisions.rationale: Close Combat is a guaranteed KO on Mega Tyranitar from its shown HP if it does not Protect, removing the immediate Rock Slide threat. Venusaur Protect preserves its valuable Grass pressure and denies Gholdengo/Tyranitar’s likely attempt to finish it while Tauros acts first.
decisions.notebook: Tauros’s exact 162 Attack Close Combat is a guaranteed KO on Mega Tyranitar at 50% across legal opposing bulk ranges, provided Protect is not active. Preserve Kingambit as the main Gholdengo answer and avoid exposing it unsupported to Arcanine. Venusaur is important long-term pressure into opposing Water types; use Protect to preserve it when it is in immediate KO range. Mega Tyranitar has sand-boosted special bulk, so Venusaur’s Giga Drain is generally a two-hit route rather than a standalone OHKO.

decisions.rationale: Shadow Ball guarantees Venusaur’s KO unless it Protects, while switching Tyranitar to Whimsicott avoids Tauros’s super-effective pressure and preserves the Mega. Whimsicott’s Grass typing blocks Sleep Powder, and Tauros’s Close Combat cannot affect Gholdengo.
decisions.notebook: Preserve Mega Tyranitar when opposing Grass- and Fighting-type pressure can combine. Gholdengo’s Steel pressure is reliable, but track Make It Rain’s Special Attack drops. Whimsicott’s Grass typing prevents powder sleep. Avoid Electric attacks while Lightning Rod is present; preserve Arcanine for endgame positioning.

decisions.rationale: Close Combat guarantees the KO on Mega Tyranitar from 50% if it does not Protect. Switch Venusaur out rather than risk its reduced-success Protect at 25%; Kingambit safely absorbs Make It Rain and preserves Venusaur for the opposing Water-types.
decisions.notebook: Tauros’s exact 162 Attack Close Combat guarantees a KO on Mega Tyranitar from 50% across legal bulk if Protect is inactive. Kingambit is the primary Gholdengo answer: spread Make It Rain into it is only 17.9–39.4%. Preserve Venusaur for long-term Water-type pressure; avoid exposing Kingambit unsupported to Arcanine.

decisions.rationale: Encore Tauros into its revealed Close Combat, making it harmless against Gholdengo’s immunity and Whimsicott’s resistance. Make It Rain then pressures both foes while reliably finishing weakened Venusaur, with spread damage improving the endgame despite Gholdengo’s Special Attack drop.
decisions.notebook: Mega Tyranitar should be preserved when Grass and Fighting pressure can combine. Gholdengo’s Steel pressure is reliable, but track Make It Rain’s Special Attack drops. Whimsicott’s Grass typing prevents powder sleep. Avoid Electric attacks while Lightning Rod is present. Preserve Arcanine for endgame positioning.

decisions.rationale: Pass with Gholdengo and bring in Arcanine. Arcanine preserves Mega Tyranitar while immediately applying strong Fire pressure to both remaining foes, and its higher Speed gives better control against Kingambit and Venusaur.
decisions.notebook: Mega Tyranitar should generally be preserved when Grass and Fighting pressure can combine. Arcanine is valuable for endgame positioning and provides immediate Fire pressure against Grass- and Steel-type opponents. Gholdengo’s Make It Rain becomes less reliable after repeated Special Attack drops; track those drops before committing to further spread attacks.

decisions.rationale: Double-target Whimsicott to remove the Prankster speed-control/Encore threat immediately. Tauros’s Close Combat plus Kingambit’s super-effective Iron Head gives the best chance to secure the KO while Tauros can still act; leaving Whimsicott enables disruptive Tailwind or Encore lines.
decisions.notebook: Game 3 opponent reveals: Whimsicott is Focus Sash Prankster with Tailwind, Taunt, Encore, Moonblast; Gholdengo is Metal Coat Good as Gold with Make It Rain, Shadow Ball, Recover, Protect; Mega Tyranitar has Rock Slide, Crunch, Low Kick, Protect. Other open-sheet opponents: Milotic (Leftovers Competitive), Arcanine (Expert Belt Flash Fire), Basculegion (Life Orb Swift Swim). Kingambit is the principal Gholdengo answer; preserve it against Arcanine where possible. Tauros’s exact Attack Close Combat guarantees KO on Mega Tyranitar from half if it does not Protect. Preserve Venusaur for Water-type endgames when feasible.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Arcanine moves first and Flare Blitz guarantees the KO on Venusaur. Gholdengo should Protect to avoid Kingambit’s Sucker Punch, preserving both Pokémon after Venusaur is removed and forcing Kingambit into a disadvantageous endgame.
decisions.notebook: Preserve Mega Tyranitar when Grass and Fighting pressure can combine. Arcanine is a key endgame Fire attacker and positioning tool. Track Gholdengo’s Special Attack drops: repeated Make It Rain becomes unreliable, so favor targeted attacks, Protect, or Recover when appropriate.

decisions.rationale: Sleep Powder on Arcanine is the highest-upside line to remove the immediate Flare Blitz pressure on both remaining Pokémon. Kingambit should use Kowtow Cleave into the weakened Gholdengo; it has a possible KO from 60% and is the best way to preserve the favorable endgame if Arcanine falls asleep.
decisions.notebook: Game 3 confirms Arcanine is Expert Belt Flash Fire with Flare Blitz, Wild Charge, Snarl, Protect. Gholdengo’s Metal Coat Make It Rain damage at -2 SpA is modest into Kingambit, while Arcanine’s Flare Blitz is the urgent threat. Against this pairing, prioritize disabling Arcanine and have Kingambit pressure Gholdengo with Kowtow Cleave.

selection: Protect [success rate reduced: Protected last turn]
decisions.rationale: Protect Gholdengo to deny Kingambit’s Sucker Punch while Arcanine’s Flare Blitz acts and reliably KOs it. This preserves both endgame pieces despite Gholdengo’s reduced Protect success rate.
decisions.notebook: Arcanine’s Flare Blitz is a guaranteed KO on Kingambit from comparable health, even through its Chople Berry. Gholdengo’s Special Attack is heavily reduced after repeated Make It Rain, so targeted Shadow Ball is weak into Dark/Steel foes; prioritize Protect, Recover, or positioning when possible.

decisions.rationale: Protect preserves Kingambit from Arcanine’s immediate Flare Blitz pressure and is the only line that avoids risking a likely immediate loss before gaining more information.
decisions.notebook: Game 3 confirms Arcanine is Expert Belt Flash Fire with Flare Blitz, Wild Charge, Snarl, and Protect. Gholdengo is Metal Coat Good as Gold with Make It Rain, Shadow Ball, Recover, and Protect. Mega Tyranitar is Adamant with Rock Slide, Crunch, Low Kick, and Protect. Against Arcanine + Gholdengo, respect Flare Blitz as the urgent physical threat; Gholdengo’s Make It Rain becomes substantially weaker after its Special Attack drops. Kingambit’s Dark attacks provide key pressure into Gholdengo, while its Chople Berry only mitigates Fighting attacks.

decisions.rationale: Recover keeps Gholdengo safe from Sucker Punch while restoring HP, and Arcanine’s Flare Blitz is faster and guaranteed to KO Kingambit even through Chople Berry. This preserves both Pokémon if Kingambit protects again and leaves the endgame strongly favorable.
decisions.notebook: Kingambit is at 46% and has already used Protect twice; its next Protect has reduced success. Arcanine’s Flare Blitz reliably KOs it through Chople Berry. Gholdengo’s Special Attack is heavily lowered after Make It Rain, so prefer Recover, Protect, or positioning over attacks into Dark/Steel targets.

decisions.rationale: Sucker Punch into Gholdengo is the only immediate high-upside line: it acts before both foes and can heavily damage or potentially remove the 60% Gholdengo if it attacks. Arcanine cannot be KOed from 92%, while slower attacks lose to Flare Blitz.
decisions.notebook: Opponent confirmed: Arcanine is Jolly Expert Belt Flash Fire with Flare Blitz, Wild Charge, Snarl, Protect. Gholdengo is Modest Metal Coat Good as Gold with Make It Rain, Shadow Ball, Recover, Protect. Mega Tyranitar is Adamant with Rock Slide, Crunch, Low Kick, Protect. Preserve Dark pressure into Gholdengo; its repeated Make It Rain drops reduce its offensive urgency. Arcanine's Flare Blitz is the key physical threat to Steel partners. Kingambit's Chople Berry only helps against Fighting attacks.

reflections.summary: Won game 3 and the series 2-1 primarily through a strong Whimsicott/Gholdengo/Arcanine structure and disciplined endgame play: Encore constrained Tauros, Make It Rain removed Tauros and heavily weakened Kingambit, Protect preserved Gholdengo, and Arcanine’s Flare Blitz finished Venusaur and Kingambit through Chople Berry. The zero recorded decision errors mattered. Whimsicott’s utility set and Arcanine were excellent into the revealed composition; Gholdengo was useful but became attack-limited after Make It Rain. Bringing Mega Tyranitar was less clearly justified: its sand can undermine Focus Sash Whimsicott, and its value is not demonstrated in the supplied turns, so Mega Evolving it was not obviously the best preview choice. The four brought were serviceable, but the team preview could have prioritized a more direct answer to Kingambit and the Fire/Grass pressure. No prior-game decisions or explicit between-game changes are provided, so there is no evidence that a specific adjustment helped or backfired; game 3 itself was won by sound execution rather than an identifiable documented adjustment.
reflections.adjustment: Against a rematch, retain Whimsicott, Gholdengo, and Arcanine as the proven core, but reconsider automatically bringing or Mega Evolving Tyranitar because sand conflicts with Focus Sash and its matchup value was unclear. Test Basculegion or Milotic in that slot, depending on their actual sets, for stronger pressure into Kingambit, Tauros, and the opponent’s Fire options. Keep Encore and Protect sequencing central, preserve Arcanine for Kingambit, and avoid spending Gholdengo’s Make It Rain too early if its Special Attack drop leaves it unable to pressure Dark/Steel targets. Charizard-Y could pressure Venusaur but should be treated cautiously because sun also improves Chlorophyll Venusaur; Dragonite’s Tailwind and Ground coverage are plausible alternatives but are not proven superior from the supplied evidence.
reflections.notebook: Opponent revealed a Life Orb Modest Venusaur with Sleep Powder, Giga Drain, Sludge Bomb, and Protect; a Focus Sash Timid Raichu with Fake Out, Thunderbolt, Encore, and Nuzzle, supported by Lightning Rod; an Adamant Defiant Chople Berry Kingambit with Kowtow Cleave, Iron Head, Sucker Punch, and Protect; and a Jolly Intimidate Sitrus Berry Aqua Tauros with Close Combat, Raging Bull, Aqua Jet, and Protect. Respect Raichu’s disruption and Lightning Rod, avoid treating Kingambit as safe from Fire attacks because Chople does not prevent Arcanine’s Flare Blitz from KOing it, and account for Defiant before using Intimidate. Whimsicott’s Focus Sash, Prankster Encore/Taunt, and Tailwind utility fit this opponent well. Arcanine’s Jolly Expert Belt offensive set was highly effective; Gholdengo’s Protect and typing were valuable, but Make It Rain’s Special Attack drops require conservative timing. Mega Tyranitar’s sand may conflict with Whimsicott’s Sash, so reassess that slot and Mega choice rather than defaulting to it. The unused Basculegion and Milotic deserve matchup testing, while Charizard-Y and Dragonite are situational alternatives rather than automatic upgrades.

reflections.summary: The 1-2 series loss was decided by game 3's unfavorable resource trade, not recorded decision errors. Tauros was Encored into resisted Close Combat after damaging Whimsicott, then fell to Make It Rain; although Whimsicott was removed, Venusaur entered at only 25% and was immediately eliminated by Arcanine. Kingambit was then left alone against Gholdengo and Arcanine and could not convert the endgame. The preview plan was questionable: Venusaur was brought without Mega Charizard Y, leaving no demonstrated Chlorophyll support, while the remaining four had limited durable answers to the Arcanine-Gholdengo-Tyranitar core. No game 1-2 adjustment record is supplied, so it cannot be determined whether specific between-game changes helped; the game-3 bring itself backfired. Prep correctly included Kingambit and Tauros as relevant pressure, but Charizard/Venusaur synergy was not actually fielded, and there is insufficient set information to claim that Sableye, Altaria, Emolga, or Avalugg would have improved the matchup.
reflections.adjustment: For a rematch, do not bring Venusaur as a nominal Chlorophyll piece unless bringing and protecting Mega Charizard Y is part of a concrete weather plan that accounts for Mega Tyranitar; otherwise choose a four that independently pressures Gholdengo, Arcanine, and Tyranitar. If Charizard is selected, Mega Evolve it deliberately for sun and avoid exposing it freely to Tyranitar's Rock Slide. Prioritize denying or immediately punishing Whimsicott's Tailwind/Encore, avoid allowing Tauros to be locked into resisted Close Combat, and preserve a non-Steel endgame answer to Arcanine. Reassess the registered six around that requirement; the omitted Pokémon cannot be recommended from the supplied evidence because their sets and relevant matchup functions are unknown.
reflections.notebook: Opponent game-3 reveal: Whimsicott is Timid Focus Sash Prankster with Tailwind, Taunt, Encore, Moonblast; it uses Encore to create forced-move lines. Mega Tyranitar is Adamant with Rock Slide, Crunch, Low Kick, Protect. Gholdengo is Modest Metal Coat Good as Gold with Make It Rain, Shadow Ball, Recover, Protect; Make It Rain's SpA drops can lower its immediate pressure, but Recover/Protect give it staying power, and Good as Gold blocks status disruption. Arcanine is Jolly Expert Belt Flash Fire with Flare Blitz, Wild Charge, Snarl, Protect; Flare Blitz is a major threat to Steel partners. In game 3 the opponent brought Whimsicott, Mega Tyranitar, Gholdengo, and Arcanine, leaving Milotic and Basculegion out. Future prep: build an independent answer to the Arcanine-Gholdengo-Tyranitar core, respect Whimsicott speed control and Encore, and only pair Venusaur with a reliable, preservable sun plan.
